en: His main agent doesn't even touch files.

speaker: Unknown
en: Wow, it's focused on only one thing.
zh: 哇，它只专注于一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: How am I ever going to get a good answer out of this thing if the only thing it looks at is can I write the code for you right now?
zh: 如果它唯一关注的就是「我现在能为你写代码吗」，那我怎么可能从这个东西那里得到好的答案？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I just forced it to never do that again.
zh: 所以我直接强制它永远不要再那样做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: They are good at writing code, but not at engineering an application.
zh: 它们擅长写代码，但不擅长构建一个应用程序。

speaker: Unknown
en: The heap just needs to go completely.
zh: 堆就应该被彻底去掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't need pointers, we don't need dynamic memory.
zh: 我们不需要指针，不需要动态内存。

speaker: Unknown
en: If, for some reason, AI disappears, everything will fall down.
zh: 如果出于某种原因 AI 消失了，一切都会垮掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think that will happen?
zh: 你认为那会发生吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I see three things happening.
zh: 我看到三件事正在发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the single biggest thing that you would say engineering has really shifted towards, which is different than a few years ago?
zh: 你会说工程领域真正转向的最大的一件事是什么，与几年前不同的？

speaker: Unknown
en: So first, the thing that I'm seeing that I don't really like, and that is that I've seen that cooperation and coordination is starting to slip away.
zh: 首先，我看到的这件事我并不太喜欢，那就是我看到协作和协调正在开始流失。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the importance of pull requests, people working together, commenting on their own pull requests, on other people's pull requests.
zh: 拉取请求的重要性，人们一起工作，在自己和别人的拉取请求上评论。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some people are even saying a pull request might disappear.
zh: 甚至有人说拉取请求可能会消失。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what I'm seeing is a more individual way of developing and lesser cooperation.
zh: 而我看到的是一种更个人化的开发方式，更少的协作。

speaker: Unknown
en: You work together with your agents, but you don't work together with your team anymore.
zh: 你和你的智能体一起工作，但你不再和你的团队一起工作了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or at least that's the trend I'm seeing, and I think it's a dangerous trend.
zh: 或者至少那是我看到的趋势，我认为这是一个危险的趋势。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why do you think that is specifically?
zh: 你具体认为为什么会这样？

speaker: Unknown
en: And for me, I have the assumption that...
zh: 而对我来说，我有一个假设……

speaker: Unknown
en: In practice, it might be what we see online, kind of on Reddit, that's my bubble, or YouTube, because there are a lot of solo developers that are kind of on the frontier of things.
zh: 实际上，可能就是我们在线上看到的，比如 Reddit 上那种，那是我的信息茧房，或者 YouTube，因为有很多处于前沿的独立开发者。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I don't know if that resonates what happens in bigger organizations where there are still bigger teams and people collaborating with agents and each other.
zh: 但我不知道这是否符合更大组织里的实际情况，那里仍然有更大的团队，人们既和智能体协作也彼此协作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so I have the privilege of not being on any social media.
zh: 是的，所以我有幸不在任何社交媒体上。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't have a Reddit account.
zh: 我没有 Reddit 账号。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I only use LinkedIn to talk to you.
zh: 我是说，我只用 LinkedIn 和你聊天。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have absolutely zero interest in following social media, but I do read a lot and I read articles and I read white papers and I talk to a lot of companies and a lot of people in companies.
zh: 我对关注社交媒体完全没有兴趣，但我确实读很多东西，我读文章、读白皮书，我和很多公司以及公司里的很多人交谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's a difference between building something fast and not finishing it.
zh: 所以，快速构建一个东西但不把它做完，

speaker: Unknown
en: And building something that you hope will last.
zh: 和构建一个你希望经久耐用的东西，是有区别的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's that classic marathon versus sprint thing.
zh: 就是那种经典的马拉松对短跑的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And people building things by themselves usually don't push it that extra edge towards being completed.
zh: 而独自构建东西的人通常不会把它往完成的方向再推那最后一把。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is, I think, what the difference is.
zh: 我认为，这就是区别所在。

speaker: Unknown
en: Showing something on social media or on YouTube.
zh: 在社交媒体或 YouTube 上展示一个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like for example, you see a lot of people building games very fast.
zh: 比如,你会看到很多人在非常快地做游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reason why I want to do air quotes is because the biggest problem with games is listening to your users, doing the game design correctly.
zh: 而我之所以想打引号,是因为做游戏最大的问题在于倾听你的用户、正确地做游戏设计。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is still something you can iterate with your agent, but you need to communicate to the world.
zh: 这仍然是你可以用你的智能体去迭代的事情,但你需要与外部世界沟通。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think people working within their bubble, not having to communicate with other people,
zh: 所以我认为人们在自己的小泡泡里工作,不必与其他人沟通,

speaker: Unknown
en: But always was one of the most difficult things to do.
zh: 但这一直是最困难的事情之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's only being enforced now because you can you can show a lot of progress but you do that by yourself and
zh: 我认为这一点现在只是被强化了,因为你可以展示很多进展,但这些都是你自己一个人做出来的,而且

speaker: Unknown
en: Remembering why you're building a piece of software or for whom you're building it.
zh: 记住你为什么要构建一个软件,或者你在为谁构建它。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why I said product is becoming more important.
zh: 这就是为什么我说产品变得越来越重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that is the thing that is really taking a beating right now.
zh: 我觉得这正是现在真正受到冲击的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you have any ideas on how to solve this?
zh: 你有什么解决这个问题的想法吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because
zh: 因为

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's very easy.
zh: 我觉得这很容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm in my little bubble.
zh: 我就在我自己的小泡泡里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I used to think starting things is one of the hardest things.
zh: 我过去认为开始做事情是最难的事情之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was it for me.
zh: 对我来说就是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now I've started many things and I've never finished it.
zh: 现在我已经开始了很多事情,而且从来没有完成过。

speaker: Unknown
en: People used to tell me that and I was like, I don't get it.
zh: 人们过去这么告诉我,我会说,我不明白。

speaker: Unknown
en: I only start when I'm able to finish it.
zh: 我只有在我能完成的时候才会开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now starting has never become this easy for me.
zh: 现在,开始对我来说从来没有变得这么容易过。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yep.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even with my license, I have credits.
zh: 即使是我的 license,我有 credits。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm like, oh, I have this little bar, and at the end of the month, I want my bar, or at the end of the week, I want my bar to be as close to 100% as I can.
zh: 我会说,哦,我有这样一个小进度条,在月底,我想要我的进度条,或者在周末,我希望我的进度条尽可能接近 100%。

speaker: Unknown
en: So before I go to bed, I'm like, what can I build?
zh: 所以在我睡觉之前,我会想,我能构建点什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: A game.
zh: 一个游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've definitely built games.
zh: 我确实做过游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: I built a harness that builds games so other people can build games.
zh: 我构建了一个能做游戏的 harness,这样其他人就可以做游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like one meta layer.
zh: 这就像是往上多了一层元层面。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm trying to solve problems that I think are gonna happen in the future and seeing kind of what the results are of those.
zh: 我在尝试解决那些我认为未来会发生的问题,并看看这些的结果如何。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then...
zh: 但是然后……

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't take the extra mile.
zh: 我不会多走那额外的一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't harden it.
zh: 我不会把它加固打磨。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't finish it.
zh: 我不会完成它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't build this out to become a product that I then sell.
zh: 我不会把它构建成一个我然后拿去卖的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: I start many things.
zh: 我开始很多事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't finish many things.
zh: 我完成不了很多事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that was always the case.
zh: 但这一直都是如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I have built, gosh, five compilers.
zh: 所以我做过,天哪,五个编译器。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've started them all.
zh: 我全部都开始了。

speaker: Unknown
en: They all were almost finished.
zh: 它们全都已经接近完成。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's only one I can say was actually finished.
zh: 而只有一个我可以说真正完成了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so starting things and not finishing them was always a part of software development because you have a cool idea, you want to learn, you start building.
zh: 所以开始做事情而不完成它们,一直是软件开发的一部分,因为你有一个很酷的想法,你想学习,你就开始构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: The only difference now is why are you starting the project?
zh: 现在唯一的区别是,你为什么要开始这个项目?

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you starting the project to learn or to experiment with the agents or to actually build a product?
zh: 你是为了学习、或者为了和智能体做实验,还是为了真正构建一个产品而开始这个项目?

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think the intention behind what you're going to be doing in the future needs to harden.
zh: 所以我认为,你未来要做的事情背后的意图需要变得坚定。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as soon as that intention hardens, that question you just asked goes away a little bit.
zh: 而一旦那个意图变得坚定,你刚才问的那个问题就会稍微消失一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if the intention is to just have fun, man, you've already reached your goal.
zh: 所以如果意图只是玩得开心,伙计,你已经达到了你的目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: If the intention is to build a company out of it, then you need to finish something.
zh: 如果意图是从中创建一家公司,那你就需要完成一些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then for people that are experiencing this, me and my agent, we're kind of in a bubble.
zh: 而对于那些正在经历这种情况的人,我和我的智能体,我们有点像是在一个泡泡里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if I have a question, instead of going and reaching out to you, I would ask my agent.
zh: 如果我有一个问题,与其去找你沟通,我会去问我的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's kind of the way of working that I see, at least in my environment.
zh: 这是我所看到的一种工作方式，至少在我的环境里是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: What would your advice be for people to step out of that and start collaborating more?
zh: 你会给大家什么建议，让他们走出这种状态，开始更多地协作？

speaker: Unknown
en: To be really honest, I've been thinking about this for a very long time.
zh: 说实话，这个问题我已经想了很久了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the way we work together and the way we build software has to change.
zh: 我认为我们合作的方式和构建软件的方式必须改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you've had this open source movement for a very long time.
zh: 你看，开源运动已经存在了很久。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we need to have focus more on things like meetups, sharing information, sharing knowledge, working together.
zh: 我认为我们需要更专注于聚会、分享信息、分享知识、一起合作这类事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Have groups that want to review each other's products.
zh: 组建一些愿意互相评审产品的团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, we need to really come together and work together.
zh: 我的意思是，我们需要真正地走到一起，一起合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that means that even though it is easier to stay in your own bubble,
zh: 这意味着，尽管待在自己的小圈子里更容易，

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we need to find a way how to lower that bar of finding people who are just curious about what you're doing.
zh: 但我认为我们需要找到一种方法，降低门槛，去找到那些对你正在做的事情感到好奇的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that also means we need to be a little bit more open and not so afraid to give our ideas away because ideas are, people always say that ideas are cheap, but they don't feel cheap to the person having the idea.
zh: 这也意味着我们需要更开放一些，不要那么害怕把自己的想法分享出去，因为想法——人们总是说想法很廉价，但对拥有那个想法的人来说，它们并不廉价。

speaker: Unknown
en: They are cheap in the global scheme of things, but they feel personal.
zh: 在全局层面上它们确实廉价，但它们感觉是很个人化的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So sharing an idea and that fear that somebody else is going to run away with it or you did something wrong or stuff like that, I think that is the thing we need to focus on by building a very inclusive community.
zh: 所以分享一个想法，以及那种担心别人会把它带走、或者自己哪里做错了之类的恐惧，我认为这就是我们需要通过建立一个非常有包容性的社区来解决的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the coolest example I can give is, I don't know if you know World of Warcraft Forever that just came out.
zh: 我能给出的最棒的例子是，我不知道你知不知道刚推出的 World of Warcraft Forever。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, when you go into the beta and you just ask a silly question, how do I turn off this setting?
zh: 我是说，当你进入 beta 版，问一个愚蠢的问题，比如怎么关掉这个设置？

speaker: Unknown
en: You get four or five people helping you.
zh: 你会得到四五个人的帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the feeling we need to have, but then for people who want to build software.
zh: 这就是我们需要的氛围，只不过是针对那些想构建软件的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If the trend I see is that you would ask your agent, right?
zh: 我看到的一个趋势是，你会去问你的智能体，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no reason to ask a human because also some people don't have patience in general for people asking questions which they think are silly.
zh: 没有理由去问人类，而且有些人通常也没有耐心去回答他们认为愚蠢的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've heard people say, ask your agent first before asking me, which is, it's kind of funny in a very horrible way.
zh: 我听过有人说，先问你的智能体，再来问我，这话说起来挺搞笑的，但也很可怕。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that is what people are doing now.
zh: 但这就是人们现在在做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're more in isolation.
zh: 他们更加孤立了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Imposter syndrome has never been a bigger thing, I feel like.
zh: 我感觉冒名顶替综合征从来没有这么严重过。

speaker: Unknown
en: And people rely on their agents to give them guidance even though they might be steered in the wrong direction or they might not see kind of the bigger picture or even from a learning perspective might not learn as much when interacting with agents instead of humans.
zh: 人们依赖他们的智能体来给他们指引，即使他们可能被带向错误的方向，或者看不到更大的图景，甚至从学习的角度来说，与智能体互动而不是与人互动，可能学不到那么多东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, humans, it is slower to ask a human because you will not get an immediate answer.
zh: 我是说，问人类确实更慢，因为你不会立刻得到答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: But agents tend to want to give you the answer you want to hear.
zh: 但智能体倾向于给你想听的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can solve a little bit of that by having multiple models you can talk to and then challenge each other and you can do some harness things like adversarial setups and so you can do things but what happens is that
zh: 你可以通过同时和多个模型对话来部分解决这个问题，让它们互相挑战，你还可以做一些工具层面的东西，比如对抗性设置等等，你可以做这些事，但结果是

speaker: Unknown
en: You will only start to communicate with these machines that are very fast to answer and you will not take the time to sit by yourself with your own thoughts.
zh: 你只会开始和这些回答非常快的机器交流，而不会花时间独自坐下来，与自己的思绪相处。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just let the chaos of the world go through your head until you find a little bit of clarity that you can use to have a good idea or to know how to do things differently.
zh: 让世界的混乱在你脑中流淌，直到你找到一点清晰感，让你能产出一个好想法，或者知道如何用不同的方式做事。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can go into how I write software with agents as well, but I think that that original idea of creativity, like John Cleese said, the open and the closed creativity, the open one needs a state, a mental state of being open.
zh: 我们也可以聊聊我是怎么用智能体写软件的，但我觉得那个关于创造力的最初理念，就像 John Cleese 说的，开放式创造力和封闭式创造力，开放的那种需要一种状态，一种敞开的心理状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you only get that by
zh: 而你只有通过

speaker: Unknown
en: By being at peace, by not doing anything, by letting all that chaos out of your head.
zh: 通过保持平静，什么都不做，让所有的混乱从你脑中释放出来，才能获得那种状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: And with that continuous stream of information that social media is giving you and AI is giving you and your agents are giving you and all of that kind of stuff, there is no more moment to just sit there, close your eyes and
zh: 而随着社交媒体给你的、AI 给你的、你的智能体给你的那股源源不断的信息流，再也没有那种时刻可以只是坐在那里，闭上眼睛，

speaker: Unknown
en: Get to know yourself.
zh: 去认识你自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the downside of that?
zh: 那样做的坏处是什么？
